ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the figure is the power supply E, and the wires on the left and right sides form an outer loop. In the upper branch, the left capacitor C1 and the right capacitor C2 are connected in series, with a node in the middle marked as a black dot. This middle node also branches downward, passes through switch S and then capacitor C3, and finally connects to the right-side wire node. In the figure, switch S is drawn in the open state; the problem states that the three capacitors are identical. Reasoning: When switch S is open, the lower branch containing C3 is not connected, so C3 does not participate in the circuit. At this time, C1 and C2 are two identical capacitors connected in series across the two ends of power supply E, and the voltage is evenly distributed, so the voltage across C1 is E/2. After switch S is closed, C3 is connected in, and it is connected between the middle node of C1 and C2 and the right-side node, on the same pair of nodes as C2, so C2 and C3 are in parallel, and the equivalent capacitance is 2C. Thus the circuit becomes the capacitance C of C1 connected in series with the equivalent capacitance 2C across the two ends of power supply E. The charges in the series branch are equal, the total equivalent capacitance is (C·2C)/(C+2C)=2C/3, and the charge Q=(2C/3)E. Thus the voltage on C1 is Q/C=2E/3. Since 2E/3 is greater than E/2, after the switch is closed, the voltage across C1 increases.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, the three capacitors are identical. When switch \(S\) is closed, how does the voltage across \(C_1\) change?

method.method_draft: First identify the topology from the image before and after closing the switch. With S open, ignore C3 because its branch is disconnected; C1 and C2 are identical capacitors in series across the source E, so the source voltage divides equally and VC1=E/2. With S closed, C3 is connected between the same two nodes as C2, so C2||C3 has capacitance 2C. Now C1 is in series with an equivalent 2C capacitor across E. Use series charge equality: Ceq=(C·2C)/(C+2C)=2C/3, Q=Ceq E=2CE/3, so VC1=Q/C=2E/3. Since 2E/3>E/2, the voltage across C1 increases.

method.method_draft: From the image, set the battery rails as fixed potentials: left rail E and right rail 0. With S open, only C1 and C2 are active in series; by symmetry their common node is at E/2, so the initial voltage across C1 is E/2. When S closes, the central node becomes connected also to the left plate of C3. Let the new central-node potential be V. The conductor group at this node is isolated from the battery terminals except through capacitor dielectrics, so its total free charge is conserved; using the initially neutral middle-node group, sum the charges on the three plates attached to it: C(V−E)+C(V)+C(V)=0. Solve V=E/3, so the final voltage across C1 is E−E/3=2E/3. Compare to E/2 and conclude that the voltage across C1 increases.

图像描述：图中底部是电源 E，左侧导线可视为左电源轨，右侧导线可视为右电源轨；上方 C1 与 C2 串联，二者中间有一个黑点节点。C3 位于下方支路，其右端接到右侧电源轨，左端通过开关 S 接到 C1、C2 之间的中间节点。图中开关 S 初始是断开的，题目问闭合 S 后 C1 两端电压如何变化。

推理：按图中电源取左电源轨电势为 E，右电源轨电势为 0。S 断开时，参与回路的只有相同的 C1 与 C2 串联，因此中间节点电势由对称性为 E/2，所以 C1 初始电压为 E - E/2 = E/2。S 闭合后，中间节点还连接到 C3 的左极板。设新的中间节点电势为 V。该导体组不与电源端直接导通，只通过电容介质相连，所以该导体组总自由电荷守恒，且初始总电荷为 0。闭合后的中间导体组连接了 C1 的右极板、C2 的左极板和 C3 的左极板，因此有 C(V - E) + C(V - 0) + C(V - 0) = 0。解得 3V - E = 0，即 V = E/3。于是 C1 最终电压为 E - E/3 = 2E/3。因为 2E/3 大于 E/2，所以 C1 两端电压增大。
